children: American Eagle Outfitters said merchandise margins shrank in the second quarter, as its core brand is slow to return to growth.

Merchandise margins shed 3.3 percentage points due to promotional markdowns at American Eagle's namesake brand, which offset improvement in Aerie. Executives said it is still trying to offload some of its older inventory at a discount because fashion trends have made such a sharp pivot.
"We're moving in the right direction, yet there remains work to do," Chief Executive Jay Schottenstein told analysts on a call Wednesday.
Shares dropped 10% to $15.20 in after-hours trading.
Second-quarter total same-store sales rose 6%, just behind the 6.7% growth that Wall Street projected. Same-store sales at the American Eagle core brand fell 1%.

Women's jeans styles shifted dramatically to lower-waisted and baggier fits, and now the company is trying to adjust its inventory to match that. It still has a lot of older jeans that it is trying to sell while it introduces trendier items, executives said.
"What we are needing to work through right now is just some of the older fits and really just rebalancing our inventory," said Jennifer Foyle, president and executive creative director.
Aerie, which specializes in underwear and bras, has become especially important for American Eagle because the company's core business has been underperforming.
Same-store sales were up 19% for Aerie, following two quarters of more than 20% growth.
Total revenue for the second quarter rose 8% to $1.38 billion. Analysts surveyed by FactSet forecast revenue of $1.37 billion.
Profit was $134.1 million, or 79 cents a share, up from $77.6 million, or 45 cents a share, a year earlier. Analysts anticipated 22 cents a share.
The company received $196 million in tariff refunds, which benefited second-quarter results and are included in its new guidance.
American Eagle now expects operating income for 2026 to be $540 million to $550 million, up from a previous range of $390 million to $410 million.
In the current third quarter, the retailer expects same-store sales will increase by a mid-to-high single digit percentage. Analysts were forecasting a 3.7% increase.
